title: Understanding and Applying the Scrum Framework
description: Begin with the framework, then reason about what transparency and adaptation require in a real decision.

areas.title: Empiricism
areas.description: Make assumptions visible and change decisions when evidence changes.

areas.title: Scrum Values
areas.description: Connect commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage to observable team behavior.

areas.title: Scrum Team
areas.description: Distinguish shared product accountability from the three specific accountabilities.

areas.title: Events
areas.description: Explain the inspection and adaptation purpose of each event instead of memorizing meeting names.

areas.title: Artifacts
areas.description: Use artifacts and commitments to make product work inspectable.

areas.title: Done
areas.description: Keep a shared quality boundary and distinguish it from item-specific acceptance criteria.

areas.title: Scaling
areas.description: Reason from one product, shared direction and an integrated usable Increment.

title: Developing People and Teams
description: Understand decision ownership and productive collaboration. The links below are starting points, not a claim of complete proficiency in every focus area.

areas.title: Self-Managing Teams
areas.description: Create clarity about goals and boundaries while letting the team decide how to work.

areas.title: Facilitation
areas.description: Help people inspect common evidence and reach a transparent product decision.

areas.title: Leadership Styles
areas.description: Examine authority, autonomy and the consequences of acting as a request proxy.

areas.title: Coaching
areas.description: A separate focus area for developing others; no dedicated coaching lesson is published yet.

areas.title: Mentoring
areas.description: A separate focus area for sharing experience; no dedicated mentoring lesson is published yet.

areas.title: Teaching
areas.description: A separate focus area for helping people understand concepts; no dedicated teaching lesson is published yet.

title: Managing Products with Agility
description: Connect direction, value, customer evidence and ordering decisions across the life of a product.

areas.title: Forecasting & Release Planning
areas.description: Communicate what historical evidence supports and where a forecast remains uncertain.

areas.title: Product Vision
areas.description: Explain the audience, need and direction before committing to a fixed feature list.

areas.title: Product Value
areas.description: Distinguish outputs from outcomes and inspect current and unrealized value.

areas.title: Product Backlog Management
areas.description: Refine useful slices and compare value, risk, size and dependencies.

areas.title: Business Strategy
areas.description: Use goals and experiments to guide investment under uncertainty.

areas.title: Stakeholders & Customers
areas.description: Distinguish stakeholder feedback from evidence of actual customer outcomes.

title: Developing and Delivering Products Professionally
description: A Product Owner needs enough understanding of quality, risk and flow to make sound product trade-offs without taking over implementation decisions.

areas.title: Emergent Software Development
areas.description: Learn through small integrated changes instead of assuming every detail is known up front.

areas.title: Managing Technical Risk
areas.description: Expose integration, maintenance and quality risks when comparing investment choices.

areas.title: Continuous Quality
areas.description: Treat shared quality as part of creating usable value throughout the Sprint.

areas.title: Continuous Integration
areas.description: Connect integrated evidence to a usable product instead of independent component completion.

areas.title: Continuous Delivery
areas.description: Remove artificial release gates while respecting quality and operational constraints.

areas.title: Optimizing Flow
areas.description: Use WIP, Cycle Time, Work Item Age, Throughput and an SLE to inspect flow.

title: Evolving the Agile Organization
description: Look beyond the team for incentives, overloaded portfolios and decision delays that constrain value.

areas.title: Organizational Design and Culture
areas.description: Inspect whether organizational structures and incentives support product autonomy.

areas.title: Portfolio Planning
areas.description: Make competing investments and too much parallel work visible.

areas.title: Evidence-Based Management
areas.description: Relate goals, hypotheses and experiments to CV, UV, T2M and A2I.
